rows.title: Deleting a résumé from the Dashboard silently removes every saved design that only that résumé held
rows.summary: Now: deleting a résumé keeps every saved design that only it held. The designs move to the most recently edited résumé that is left, or to a letter when no résumé is left. That record goes a version on, so the cloud sync carries the design to other devices. The design stays under Design → Template → Your designs and on /new. A design another record still holds, or one deleted (R3-008 tombstone), is left as it is. The fix is in the store's deleteResume (src/hooks/useResumeSyncActions.js), using a new designsOnlyIn helper in src/constants/templatePresets.js.
rows.product_call: The designs go to the most recently edited résumé that is left, and the delete prompt is unchanged. The other option, an account-level list of saved designs, would be a data-model change.
rows.remaining: When the last record is deleted, nothing is left to hold its designs, so they still go. A deletion that arrives from another device through the sync does not go through deleteResume, so it does not move the designs.

rows.title: Browser Back from the editor (or from Job Tracker/Projects) returns to the Dashboard at the top, not where the user had scrolled
rows.summary: Now: Back or Forward to a page returns the window to where that visit was scrolled. RouteFrame in src/AppRoutes.jsx records each history entry's window offset (by key and path, as useScrollMemory does for the workspace <main>) from the window's scroll events, so it is the offset before the editor's fixed layout clamped it. On a POP to an entry it left scrolled, RouteFrame calls window.scrollTo with that offset. A new visit (PUSH) still opens at the top, and a change of the search alone still does not move the scroll. The follow-up commit d23d3f1 keeps R2-073's contract for everything else: an entry left at its top, or never recorded, is still left to the browser. This stops a stale 0 filed under HashRouter's shared 'default' key from resetting a Back (tests/pdf/89-app-routes 'Back and Forward leave the scroll to the browser' failed without it).
rows.remaining: HashRouter gives the key 'default' to the first entry and to every address typed into the bar. So a typed address to a path the first entry showed can get that entry's non-zero offset back (useScrollMemory has the same limit). The commit message of d23d3f1 overstates this: it says a reused key brings back no old offset, but only a zero offset is left to the browser. No Playwright spec covers real browser Back. The fix is checked in node over the fake DOM.

rows.title: A PDF/Word import started on the Dashboard that finishes after the user signs out adds that person's résumé to the signed-out browser's list
rows.summary: Now: the Dashboard's document import records the account the list belonged to (syncedUid) when the file was picked. If the list has left that account by the time the read ends (signed out, or another account signed in), store.importResume({ account }) does not add the résumé to the list. It keeps it in stashed[uid], the way leaveAccount keeps unsent work, and that account's next sign-in sends it (src/hooks/useResumeStore.js). The Dashboard (src/pages/Dashboard.jsx) opens nothing and says the file was kept for that account, and importDocument (src/utils/importDocument.js) skips navigate when importResume answers null. An import with no sign-out is unchanged. A list that was never synced (signed out from the start) still takes the import.
rows.product_call: The notice says 'You signed out while … was being read', including in the rarer case where another account signed in during the read.
rows.remaining: The editor's Import (useEditorExports) does not pass `account`. It navigates within the editor, and the editor leaves the page on sign-out, but the store call would still append after a sign-out that happens in another route.

rows.title: After a cover letter is opened, the Dashboard's Career History switches to the oldest résumé instead of the one the user was working on
rows.summary: Now: when the open record is not among the résumés the panel gets (a letter is open), CareerHistoryPanel (src/components/CareerHistoryPanel.jsx) shows the résumé edited last (letterSources order), not resumes[0], the oldest. When the open record is a résumé, that résumé is still the one shown. The Dashboard and the Job Tracker both use the panel.
rows.product_call: The fallback is the résumé edited most recently, not the last one opened. The store does not record which résumé was opened last, and a letter does not record its source.
rows.remaining: A résumé that was only viewed, not edited, before a letter was opened is not remembered. If another résumé was edited more recently, that one shows.

issuesFound: R5-HUNT6-DASH-IMPORT-AFTER-SIGN-OUT was fixed on the Dashboard only: the editor's Export menu > Import of a PDF/Word file (useEditorExports.handleImportFile) still called store.importResume without `account`, so a read ending after sign-out added the résumé to the signed-out browser's list and opened it.

d23d3f1's commit message overstates its effect (a reused 'default' history key can still bring back a non-zero offset saved for that path); pushed history is not rewritten, and the row's 'remaining' already says so.

Back-scroll: HashRouter gives key 'default' to the first entry and to typed addresses / plain href='#/' links (PublicResume's footer link), so such a visit to '/' can get the first entry's saved offset back instead of the top. Rare edge, noted, not blocking.
issuesFixed: b6fe122: the editor's document import now goes through the same importingFor helper (src/utils/importDocument.js) as the Dashboard's: Editor.jsx passes the list's account (syncedUid) to useEditorExports, a late read is stashed for that account, nothing opens, and the Export menu says why. Test tests/pdf/104-r5-hunt6-dash-editor-import-after-sign-out.test.mjs (real store + real useEditorExports).
open: Non-blocking: the 'default'-key Back-scroll edge above; the delete fix does not move designs when the deletion arrives by sync or when the last record is deleted; Career History falls back to the most recently edited résumé, not the last one opened (product limits already in the rows' 'remaining').
checked: Commit author/committer on every commit: sairamgudiputi <sairamgudiputi8@gmail.com>, no trailers, no AI mention.
No existing test was changed or weakened (the diff adds test files only).
importResume's stash merges into an existing stashed[uid] (leaveAccount keeps `was`), so earlier unsent work is not lost.
designsOnlyIn counts tombstones on other records as held, so a deleted design is not revived; the Job Tracker's CareerHistoryPanel is unaffected when the open record is in its list.
